title: Simple current mirror
description: A K:1 current mirror sized as unit devices: the diode-connected reference is the library's NMOS bias reference, its programmed current delivered by an ideal source and its drain wired to its gate (its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$, so the table is read along that diagonal), and the output device is sized width-first at K times the reference width, on the reference's own $V_{GS}$ — the gate wire the two share, stated as the sizing rather than approximated by typing one inversion level into both — evaluated at the served output node's $V_{DS}$. The systematic error is then the $\lambda$ mismatch between the two drain voltages and nothing else; the random error is the Pelgrom spread of the ratio.

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves

params.name: L
params.note: longer L: lower lambda (systematic) error and more matching area

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: reference inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens current matching but costs compliance headroom. The output device inherits it through the shared gate rather than being told it separately

params.name: err_target
params.note: systematic (lambda) error budget; cascode the mirror if this cannot close

equations.name: sys_err
equations.note: lambda mismatch between the output vds and the diode point

equations.name: irel_out
equations.note: the OUTPUT device's own inversion level, read back from its operating point. It sits on the reference's gate but its own drain, so it is not the authored gm_id_m unless the two drains happen to agree

equations.name: sigma_ratio
equations.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output resistance the mirror presents: the output device's own r_o and nothing more. That is the whole cost of the simple mirror — the output current tracks the node voltage through gds, which is what the systematic-error equation measures at one particular V_out. This is the number a stage loading the mirror sees
